clue.text: It brings everything to a halt. That's the point

definitions.text: It brings everything to a halt
definitions.meaning: a dead stop that ends all movement
the dot ending a sentence is a point, or period

explanation.surface: Someone declaring a final, unarguable stop to proceedings.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share the idea of a complete stop: a total halt, and the punctuation dot that closes a sentence.

clue.text: Don is a common man

definitions.meaning: a university teacher, a member of a college's senior body
an everyday chap or guy

explanation.surface: A university academic is an ordinary chap.
explanation.definitionFit: A college teacher holds this rank at Oxford or Cambridge, and the word is also everyday slang for a chap.

clue.text: Is he one who wants more time?

definitions.text: Is he one who wants more time?

parts.words: Is he one who wants more time?
parts.note: read as a person who yearns, and also as the comparative of long, meaning lasting more time

explanation.surface: Someone asking for an extension.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who yearns is one who longs; and the comparative of long describes something lasting more time.

clue.text: Understanding the function of the pupil

definitions.meaning: realising, as in grasping a point
the pupil of the eye lets in light so we have sight

explanation.surface: Comprehension being the job of a schoolchild.
explanation.definitionFit: Grasping an idea is perceiving it; and the eye's pupil exists for vision.

clue.text: Ecstatic at leaving the trenches behind

definitions.meaning: wildly excessive in emotion
in the First World War soldiers went out of the trench and across the parapet to attack

explanation.surface: Overjoyed to get out of the trenches.
explanation.definitionFit: Being excessively thrilled is going beyond normal limits; WWI soldiers climbing out of trenches went across the parapet.

clue.text: Let the learner driver get relaxed

parts.note: L is the plate shown by a learner driver

explanation.surface: Letting a nervous learner driver calm down at the wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: To let a property is to rent it out, which is what a landlord has done once it is leased.

clue.text: Vote in Reagan if you want a spin off from atomic energy

definitions.text: a spin off from atomic energy

parts.note: to elect is to vote in
Ronald Reagan, US president, is known as Ron

explanation.surface: Voting for Reagan to gain from the nuclear industry.
explanation.definitionFit: This subatomic particle has a quantum property called spin and comes from within the atom.

clue.text: Is Patrick Moore top of the bill?

definitions.text: Is Patrick Moore top of the bill?

parts.words: Is Patrick Moore top of the bill?
parts.note: the astronomer is someone whose bent is toward the heavens, while the phrase also means the headline act of a show

explanation.surface: Asking whether a TV astronomer is headlining the show.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Patrick Moore was a long-serving British TV astronomer, presenter of The Sky at Night.
explanation.definitionFit: The main act headlining a variety show; and an astronomer's leaning is toward the heavens.

clue.text: Act a central role then quit

indicators.note: central says the role is placed at the centre of the act

parts.note: a part is a role in a play

explanation.surface: An actor plays a lead role then walks out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'central' tells you the role sits at the heart of the act, splitting it into two halves DE and ED.
explanation.definitionFit: To have quit a place is to have left it.

clue.text: Hung about for a pound in inordinate greed

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling, from Latin libra

indicators.note: inordinate means disordered, so the letters of the word after it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone lingering over a single pound out of excessive greed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inordinate' scrambles GREED into GERED; 'for' is only a link, and 'in' is kept as it stands rather than signalling a container.
explanation.definitionFit: To hang about is to stay on and loiter, a synonym phrase for having dawdled.

clue.text: Minister meets a constituency member to patch things up

parts.note: REV, Reverend, is a title of a church minister
an MP is the Member of Parliament for a constituency

explanation.surface: A clergyman meets the local MP to settle their differences.
explanation.definitionFit: To revamp is to renovate or overhaul, giving a patched-up, refreshed version.

clue.text: Enduring music written for public consumption

definitions.meaning: an unstopped, ringing note held on an open string or pipe
a message addressed openly, like an open letter, for all to read

explanation.surface: A lasting piece of music composed for a broad audience.
explanation.definitionFit: Musically, an unstopped string sounds a sustained tone; as writing, an unsealed message meant for everyone to read.

clue.text: He says it's an old coin

definitions.meaning: one who states something, a declarer
a gold or silver coin of ancient Greece

explanation.surface: A man claiming a coin is antique.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who declares is one who states; separately, the ancient Greek coin of that name.

clue.text: Begin to bake a pie around the first of September

parts.note: to bake a cake is to make it

indicators.note: the first of picks the opening letter of the month

explanation.surface: Starting to bake a pie at the beginning of September.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' only places the month's opening letter next to the pie, S just before TART, not inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To begin something is to get it going, the idiom for commencing.

clue.text: Head for curricular development task

definitions.meaning: to steer towards a destination
the job of designing a programme of study for a school or college

explanation.surface: A teacher heading off to work on the curriculum.
explanation.definitionFit: Steering towards somewhere means plotting a route; designing classes for a syllabus is building a programme of study.

clue.text: Where the cat sat in the dog house

definitions.meaning: the old reading-primer sentence about a cat and a rug
in trouble, called up for a reprimand, originally in the army

explanation.surface: A cat sitting in the dog's kennel.
explanation.definitionFit: Children's primers seat the cat on a rug; and being in the doghouse is facing a telling-off.

clue.text: Fetes relatives with peaches and cream?

explanation.surface: Family gatherings at fetes with a summer fruit dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: A peaches-and-cream complexion is a pale, rosy one; the question mark flags the description by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A complexion described as peaches and cream is pale and rosy.

clue.text: Expressions of praise in the back of the stalls

definitions.text: Expressions of praise in the back of the stalls

indicators.note: in says the praise is placed within the seats at the rear

parts.note: the pit was the rear part of the theatre stalls

explanation.surface: Applause coming from the cheap seats at the back.
explanation.walkthrough: In older theatres the pit was the cheap area at the back of the stalls; the whole clue also describes an audience's applause.
explanation.definitionFit: Enthusiastic applause and acclaim, the kind an audience gives from the stalls.

clue.text: Five balls are almost finished

definitions.meaning: in cricket an over is six balls, so five deliveries leave it one short
close to the end

explanation.surface: A cricket over winding down with five deliveries bowled.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, an over is a set of six balls bowled from one end.
explanation.definitionFit: Five deliveries are one short of a complete set of six in cricket; generally, something close to its end.

clue.text: A lover on fire!

parts.note: an old flame is a former lover

explanation.surface: A passionate lover burning with desire.
explanation.definitionFit: Ablaze, burning: the literal sense of something on fire.

clue.text: A tenor arrangement highly embellished

indicators.note: an arrangement reorders the letters, as music is reworked

explanation.surface: A tenor's elaborate musical arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Elaborately decorated, fancy and showy.

clue.text: Declare record turnover like a shot

indicators.note: turnover means the combined words are flipped round and read backwards

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: Announcing a record's sales figures in an instant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turnover' reverses TELL plus EP as one run.
explanation.definitionFit: A small ball of lead fired from a shotgun is shot.

clue.text: Firm anything but down even though short of cash

parts.note: the opposite of down is up

explanation.surface: A company doing well yet still strapped for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Being hard up is an idiom for being poor and lacking money.

clue.text: Refuse CO0 agitating to send the troops in

indicators.note: agitating means stirring up, so the letters of the words before it are shaken into a new order

parts.note: taken as written; CO is a commanding officer

explanation.surface: A commanding officer refuses to stir up trouble by deploying troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'agitating' stirs up the eight letters of REFUSE and CO; CO is a commanding officer, which helps the military surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Sending troops in is applying military might, the idiom for resorting to violence.

clue.text: Succeed in giving constructive advice

definitions.meaning: to achieve success, to get there
a suggestion to build something yourself, literally constructive

explanation.surface: Advice to succeed by building things yourself.
explanation.definitionFit: Achieving success is the idiom; and telling someone to build a thing themselves is advice that is literally constructive.

clue.text: Drop in and settle bill in total

parts.note: to pay a bill is to settle it
all means the total, the whole

explanation.surface: Popping in to clear the whole bill.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop in is to make a brief visit, the same as visiting someone socially.

clue.text: Not his style to be in the fashion

indicators.note: style suggests these letters are fashioned into a new shape

explanation.surface: Someone disowning a fashionable look as not their kind of thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'style' rearranges NOT HIS. The answer is an old word meaning stylish or modish.
explanation.definitionFit: Being stylish and modish is being in fashion.

clue.text: Most strongly inclined to split up Tess and Pete

indicators.note: split up means the two names are broken apart and their letters remixed

explanation.surface: A couple, Tess and Pete, keen to break up.
explanation.definitionFit: A slope at its most strongly inclined is the sharpest, the superlative of sheer.
